Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title "fix(fma): match Krita on Windows by its real programs.name" states the main change: the Krita Windows Fleet-maintained app now matches the installed program by its programs.name value instead of the registry key name. It is specific, names the platform and app, and matches the changeset (fuzzy_match_name added to krita.json and the generated windows.json queries updated).
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template well. It links the issue (Fixes `#58022`), explains the root cause and the fix, and records the testing done. It includes the AI section with tool and model. It also includes a changes file checkbox marked as done. Several template items remain unchecked, including automated tests, manual QA, and the Windows host validation. The description states that the queries were not run on a real Windows host, so the author disclosed this gap. The template's Frontend, database, Apple MDM, GitOps, and fleetd sections are not addressed, but most of them do not apply to this change.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#58022` requires the Krita (Windows) exists query to match an installed Krita, and the patch policy to fail on hosts with an older Krita. The root cause is the exact match on name = 'Krita_x64', which is the registry key name, not the programs.name value. The PR changes ee/maintained-apps/inputs/winget/krita.json to add "fuzzy_match_name": "Krita%". The generated ee/maintained-apps/outputs/krita/windows.json now uses name LIKE 'Krita%' in both the exists and patched queries. The publisher condition ('Krita Foundation') and the version_compare check (< '5.3.4.1') are unchanged. The patched query keeps its NOT EXISTS form, so an installed Krita with a version below 5.3.4.1 causes the patch policy to fail. The LIKE pattern matches any programs.name that begins with 'Krita', including versioned names such as 'Krita (x64) 5.2.2' from the NSIS installer. This covers the naming that the issue describes. The author verified the generated queries in SQLite only. The queries were not run on a real Windows host, so runtime behavior on Windows is not directly observed. The static query logic supports the requirement. The issue does not request automated tests, so no test requirement applies.
